notes: Host kernel 6.8.0-90-generic differs from target kernel 6.6.y; full kernel module build not performed
Userspace logic extraction harness used to test core algorithm changes
Kernel module build (make M=fs/smb/server) requires full kernel build first

contracts.detail: ksmbd_alloc_user backward compatibility: with NULL resp_ext, old and new code produce identical results (ngroups=0, sgid=NULL)
ksmbd_alloc_user with extension: correctly populates supplementary groups from resp_ext; __ksmbd_override_fsids now uses groups_alloc(user->ngroups) instead of groups_alloc(0)

behavior_differences.before: groups_alloc(0) — empty supplementary groups; files only accessible via primary group
behavior_differences.after: groups_alloc(user->ngroups) with group population — supplementary groups honored; group-owned files now accessible via SMB
behavior_differences.evidence: Test harness confirms: old override_fsids uses groups_alloc(0), new override_fsids uses groups_alloc(user->ngroups) and populates gi->gid[] from user->sgid[]

notes: Userspace harness validates algorithm logic; actual kernel credential override path not tested
1/20 assertion failed (sgid=NULL when ngroups=0) — this is a kmemdup(0) implementation detail, kernel kfree handles ZERO_SIZE_PTR and NULL both
Full validation requires running ksmbd kernel module with SMB client
Contract CT-C-001 confirms backward compatibility: old ksmbd-tools (no extension flag) produce identical behavior
Netlink protocol testing requires running kernel with ksmbd module loaded and ksmbd-tools userspace daemon
New enum values (16,17) extend protocol without breaking old tools: KSMBD_EVENT_LOGIN_REQUEST_EXT uses handle_unsupported_event, ensuring backward compatibility
resv_start_op change (16→18) informs genl subsystem of new command range
Static analysis confirms protocol extension is additive/backward compatible

blocked_or_not_run.reason: Full kernel module build requires building entire kernel (linux-6.6.y) from source, which needs 30+ minutes and produces incompatible module for host kernel 6.8.0. Running ksmbd kernel module requires QEMU VM with matching kernel version.
blocked_or_not_run.required_action: Set up QEMU VM with kernel 6.6.y and CONFIG_SMB_SERVER=y, load ksmbd module, install ksmbd-tools, run SMB client against test shares with supplementary group configurations

blocked_or_not_run.reason: PCA-0002 IOCTL_NETLINK_ABI_CHANGE requires netlink communication between kernel ksmbd module and ksmbd-tools userspace daemon. This needs a running kernel with ksmbd loaded and the userspace tools.
blocked_or_not_run.required_action: Build ksmbd-tools from source for target kernel version, install in VM, test netlink message exchange with new LOGIN_REQUEST_EXT/RESPONSE_EXT events

conclusion.rationale: Userspace logic extraction testing confirms the behavioral change in ksmbd_alloc_user and __ksmbd_override_fsids is correctly implemented. The new supplementary groups feature is backward compatible with old ksmbd-tools (NULL extension path preserves original behavior). However, full kernel module testing with actual SMB client and netlink protocol verification is required for a definitive compatibility verdict. The patch itself explicitly states backward compatibility intent, and static analysis supports this claim.
recommended_actions: Build kernel 6.6.y with CONFIG_SMB_SERVER=y and CONFIG_GCOV_KERNEL=y for coverage instrumentation
Set up QEMU VM with the instrumented kernel
Install ksmbd-tools and test with old (no-extension) and new (with-extension) tools
Create SMB share with group-only permissions and verify supplementary group access works
Run netlink trace to verify LOGIN_REQUEST_EXT/RESPONSE_EXT message exchange
Collect gcov coverage data for the patched lines in ksmbd module
